newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourse plans to simplify clearing systems.
newsitem.headline: German bourse plans to simplify clearing systems.

text.p: The German bourse operators Deutsche Boerse said on Thursday that it planned to simplify clearing conditions on the DTB futures and options exchange, to make entry into the market easier.

Direct clearing customers, who are currently only allowed to settle their own business or the business of their customers, will be allowed to take on the clearing business on behalf of related firms who are not direct clearers.
Clearing is the process by which the ownership of securities is transferred and custody is arranged.
The simplification of the clearing system will particularly help foreign participants who wish to trade on the DTB, the bourse said.
Until now, foreign banks and securities houses could not become clearing members of the DTB and had to hand their settlement business over to third-party general clearing institutions.
Under the new system, the German subsidiaries of foreign banks, who have direct clearing status, can settle business without needing to become general clearers.
Institutions are required to meet strict base capital liability requirements to become general clearers.
Under the new rules, the German subsidiaries of foreign banks no longer have to meet these requirements, thus allowing clearing to stay in-house and avoiding the need to turn to third parties.

The new rules will also help German banks, the bourse said, as related companies will no longer have to pay initial licence charges of 200,000 marks ($105,000), with an annual clearing charge of 66,000 marks.
The bourse said that the entry conditions for becoming a direct clearer will not change under the new rules.
